reason: E5 provides theoretical support for edge dislocation control in BCC HEAs via wavy structure formation, and E3/E4 show higher creep activation energy and lower creep displacement for similar HEAs versus pure W, but no cited evidence directly demonstrates edge dislocation dominance in WTaTiVZr at 800 °C or links it to improved fracture toughness, and E1/E6 do not address the specific mechanism.
premises: Severe lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr promotes edge dislocation mobility over screw dislocation mobility
Edge dislocation dominance reduces dislocation entanglement and localized strain concentrations
Pure tungsten plasticity is dominated by screw dislocations leading to lower ductility and toughness
The HEA exhibits higher creep activation energy and lower creep displacement than pure tungsten
The proposed edge dislocation mechanism applies at ~800 °C under inert atmosphere
